reference.paper: Moghe et al., Multi3NLU++ (multilingual, multi-intent, multi-domain NLU dataset)

table_12.title: In-language in-domain results for intent detection with MLP-based setup (F1 x100)
table_12.setting: Large: 10-fold cross-validation, train on 9 of 10 folds (about 1,860 messages)

threshold_rule: below 0.707 (more than 10 micro-F1 points below the lower published reference 80.7) triggers an investigation; exactly 0.707 passes

value.metric: val micro-F1 at the val-selected global θ on probabilities after the val-fitted T, compared exactly as 2TP / (2TP + FP + FN) of the summed counts

differences: a fixed split (selection train folds 0–13 with about 1,450 messages; final train folds 0–15 with about 1,658)
a fine-tuned BERTurk rather than a frozen encoder
a single split rather than cross-validation averages
this check itself reads val folds 14-15
caveats: θ and T were chosen on the same val messages, so the value is in-sample and optimistic
the paper uses a fixed θ 0.3 on frozen-encoder MLPs; neither of our numbers is like-for-like
